papers.title: Nautilus Space Observatory: Unveiling the Diversity and Origin of Sub-Neptunes with the Nautilus Space Observatory
papers.abstract: Sub-Neptunes are the most common class of planets in the Galaxy, yet they have no Solar System analog and remain poorly understood as a population. JWST observations have revealed atmospheres spanning a wide range of metallicities, compositions, and cloud properties, driving active debates over whether warm sub-Neptunes harbor liquid water oceans beneath H2-rich envelopes, maintain stratified H2/H2O interiors, or have well-mixed, metal-rich envelopes. Open questions also remain over what physical processes drive transitions between hazy and clear atmospheres. These are intrinsically population-level questions that single-target observations, however deep, cannot resolve. Here we argue that a sub-Neptune population survey with the Nautilus Space Observatory, a proposed constellation of large-diameter space telescopes, would deliver the first statistical map of sub-Neptune atmospheric diversity, test competing classification schemes, identify habitable candidates, and serve as a pathfinder population for the eventual habitable-worlds search. These goals are achievable across the proposed mission classes for the constellation, and this architecture is uniquely well-matched to this science case since population-level questions demand sample size and a uniform observing strategy.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Sub-Neptunes are planets larger than Earth but smaller than Neptune. They are the most common kind of planet in our Galaxy, yet our Solar System has none, so we have no nearby example to study. It is like knowing that most houses in the world are a certain style without ever having been inside one. Astronomers still don't know what these worlds are made of, how they formed, or whether any could be hospitable to life.

**What They Did**
This paper is a science case, not a set of new observations. The authors argue for a large survey of sub-Neptunes with the Nautilus Space Observatory, a proposed constellation of large-diameter space telescopes working together. The idea is to observe many planets with one uniform strategy, rather than studying them one at a time.

**Key Findings**
The authors start from what the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has already shown. Sub-Neptune atmospheres vary widely in their metal content (elements heavier than hydrogen and helium), their ingredients, and their clouds. This has fueled debate over what lies beneath the surface of warm sub-Neptunes. Some may hide liquid water oceans under hydrogen-rich gas. Others may have layered interiors of hydrogen and water, or thoroughly mixed, metal-rich envelopes. Scientists also don't know what makes some atmospheres hazy and others clear. The authors argue that these are questions about the whole population, and no single observation can answer them, however deep. Judging a city's climate from one street corner doesn't work. They contend that a Nautilus survey would produce the first statistical map of sub-Neptune atmospheres, test competing ways of classifying these planets, and identify potentially habitable candidates. They also say it would act as a trial run for the later search for habitable worlds, and that this is achievable across the proposed mission sizes.

**Looking Forward**
Nautilus is still a proposal, so these benefits are goals rather than results. If it is built, its large sample and consistent methods could turn scattered JWST snapshots into a coherent picture of the Galaxy's most common planets.

papers.title_tr: Nautilus Space Observatory: Nautilus Space Observatory ile Sub-Neptünlerin Çeşitliliğini ve Kökenini Ortaya Çıkarmak
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Sub-Neptünler, Dünya'dan büyük ama Neptün'den küçük gezegenlerdir. Galaksimizdeki en yaygın gezegen türüdür, ancak Güneş Sistemi'nde hiç örneği yoktur. Bu yüzden yakından inceleyebileceğimiz bir örnek elimizde bulunmuyor. Bu, dünyadaki evlerin çoğunun belli bir tarzda olduğunu bilip hiçbirinin içine girmemiş olmaya benzer. Gökbilimciler bu dünyaların neyden oluştuğunu, nasıl oluştuğunu ve hiçbirinin yaşama elverişli olup olamayacağını hâlâ bilmiyor.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Bu makale yeni gözlemlerden oluşmuyor, bir bilimsel gerekçe sunuyor. Yazarlar, birlikte çalışan büyük çaplı uzay teleskoplarından oluşan önerilmiş bir takımyıldız olan Nautilus Space Observatory ile geniş bir sub-Neptün taraması yapılması gerektiğini savunuyor. Amaç, gezegenleri tek tek incelemek yerine çok sayıda gezegeni tek tip bir gözlem stratejisiyle gözlemlemek.

**Ana Bulgular**
Yazarlar, James Webb Uzay Teleskobu'nun (JWST) şimdiden ortaya koyduklarından yola çıkıyor. Sub-Neptün atmosferleri metal içeriği (hidrojen ve helyumdan daha ağır elementler), bileşim ve bulut yapısı bakımından çok farklılık gösteriyor. Bu durum, sıcak sub-Neptünlerin yüzeyinin altında ne olduğu tartışmasını körüklüyor. Bazıları hidrojence zengin gazın altında sıvı su okyanusları barındırıyor olabilir. Bazılarının iç yapısı hidrojen ve sudan oluşan katmanlardan, bazılarının ise iyice karışmış, metalce zengin zarflardan oluşuyor olabilir. Bilim insanları ayrıca bazı atmosferlerin neden puslu, bazılarının neden berrak olduğunu da bilmiyor. Yazarlara göre bunlar tüm popülasyona dair sorular ve tek bir gözlem, ne kadar derin olursa olsun, bunları yanıtlayamaz. Bir şehrin iklimini tek bir sokak köşesinden yargılamaya benzer bu. Yazarlar, Nautilus taramasının sub-Neptün atmosferlerinin ilk istatistiksel haritasını çıkaracağını, bu gezegenleri sınıflandırmaya yönelik rakip yaklaşımları sınayacağını ve yaşanabilir olabilecek adayları belirleyeceğini savunuyor. Ayrıca taramanın, yaşanabilir dünyalar için yapılacak daha sonraki aramaya bir ön deneme işlevi göreceğini ve bunun önerilen görev ölçeklerinin hepsinde mümkün olduğunu söylüyorlar.

**İleriye Bakış**
Nautilus hâlâ bir öneri aşamasında. Bu yüzden anlatılan yararlar henüz sonuç değil, hedeftir. Teleskop inşa edilirse büyük örneklem sayısı ve tutarlı yöntemleri, dağınık JWST gözlemlerini Galaksi'nin en yaygın gezegenlerine dair bütünlüklü bir tabloya dönüştürebilir.

papers.title: Transmission Spectrum of the Benchmark Temperate Exo-Neptune TOI-1231 b
papers.abstract: The JWST is revolutionizing our understanding of the temperate sub-Neptune population through atmospheric spectroscopy. The nature of these planets remains debated, as their bulk properties are compatible with a range of interior scenarios, including mini-Neptunes, hycean worlds, and gas dwarfs, with different predicted atmospheric compositions. While theoretical studies have predicted compositional diagnostics for shallow- versus deep-atmosphere scenarios, there is a critical need for empirical constraints for a temperate planet that is a priori known to possess a deep H₂-rich atmosphere. The temperate exo-Neptune TOI-1231 b provides one such benchmark target. In this work, we present the JWST near-infrared (0.65--5.2 μm) transmission spectrum of TOI-1231 b, observed with NIRISS single-object slitless spectroscopy and NIRSpec G395H, representing the first for a temperate exo-Neptune. The density of TOI-1231 b requires a thick H₂-rich atmosphere, making the planet a keystone reference case for testing mini-Neptune scenarios for sub-Neptunes. We report a strong detection of CH₄ ( B = 54.5-69.6) and moderate to strong evidence for CO₂ ( B = 2.9-6.6). We do not find significant evidence for any other prominent molecule, although we find high 95\% upper limits on the mixing ratios of NH₃ and CO, both of which are expected in deep H₂-rich atmospheres. We also do not find any significant evidence for sulfur-bearing species that have been inferred for some temperate sub-Neptunes. This composition is consistent with expectations for a temperate Neptune possessing a deep H₂-rich atmosphere with no distinct surface. We discuss the implications of our results for the characterization of temperate sub-Neptunes.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Many of the planets we find around other stars fall between Earth and Neptune in size, and nobody is quite sure what they are made of. Some may be small versions of Neptune wrapped in thick, hydrogen-rich gas. Others might be "hycean worlds" with oceans under hydrogen skies, or rocky "gas dwarfs." Each idea predicts a different atmospheric recipe. To tell them apart, scientists need a reference case, like a calibration weight for a scale. TOI-1231 b is that reference. Its density shows it must carry a deep, hydrogen-rich atmosphere, so it gives a known answer to compare other planets against.

**What They Did**
The team used the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) to watch starlight filter through the planet's atmosphere as it passed in front of its star. Different gases absorb different colors of infrared light, leaving fingerprints in the starlight. The researchers combined two instruments, NIRISS and NIRSpec G395H, to cover wavelengths from 0.65 to 5.2 micrometers. This is the first such spectrum for a temperate Neptune-sized planet, meaning one that is mild rather than scorching.

**Key Findings**
Methane (CH₄) showed up very strongly. Carbon dioxide (CO₂) also appeared, with moderate to strong evidence. The team found no significant sign of other prominent molecules. They could only set high upper limits on ammonia and carbon monoxide, both expected in deep hydrogen-rich atmospheres, so those gases are not ruled out. They also saw no clear sign of sulfur-bearing gases, which have been suggested for some other temperate sub-Neptunes. Overall, this mix matches what scientists expect from a Neptune-like planet with a deep hydrogen atmosphere and no distinct surface underneath.

**Looking Forward**
TOI-1231 b now acts as a yardstick. When astronomers study other temperate sub-Neptunes, they can compare those results with this one to judge whether a planet looks like a mini-Neptune or something more exotic, such as an ocean world. That should make claims about these planets easier to test.

papers.title_tr: Kıyas Noktası Ilıman Ötegezegen Neptün TOI-1231 b'nin Geçiş Tayfı
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Diğer yıldızların çevresinde bulduğumuz gezegenlerin çoğu boyut olarak Dünya ile Neptün arasında yer alıyor ve bunların neyden yapıldığından kimse tam emin değil. Bazıları, kalın ve hidrojence zengin bir gaz tabakasıyla sarılı küçük Neptün'ler olabilir. Diğerleri hidrojen gökyüzünün altında okyanuslar barındıran "hiseyan dünyalar" ya da kayaç yapılı "gaz cüceleri" olabilir. Her fikir farklı bir atmosfer bileşimi öngörüyor. Bunları birbirinden ayırmak için bilim insanlarının bir referans örneğe ihtiyacı var; tıpkı bir teraziyi ayarlamak için kullanılan standart ağırlık gibi. TOI-1231 b bu referans. Yoğunluğu, gezegenin derin ve hidrojence zengin bir atmosfere sahip olması gerektiğini gösteriyor. Dolayısıyla diğer gezegenleri karşılaştırabileceğimiz bilinen bir cevap sunuyor.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, gezegen yıldızının önünden geçerken yıldız ışığının gezegenin atmosferinden süzülüşünü izlemek için James Webb Uzay Teleskobu'nu (JWST) kullandı. Farklı gazlar kızılötesi ışığın farklı renklerini soğurur ve yıldız ışığında parmak izi bırakır. Araştırmacılar, 0,65 ile 5,2 mikrometre arasındaki dalga boylarını kapsamak için NIRISS ve NIRSpec G395H adlı iki cihazı birleştirdi. Bu, Neptün boyutunda ılıman, yani kavurucu olmayan bir gezegen için elde edilen ilk bu tür tayf.

**Ana Bulgular**
Metan (CH₄) çok güçlü biçimde ortaya çıktı. Karbondioksit (CO₂) için de orta ile güçlü arası kanıt bulundu. Ekip, diğer belirgin moleküllere dair anlamlı bir iz görmedi. Derin ve hidrojence zengin atmosferlerde beklenen amonyak ve karbon monoksit için yalnızca yüksek üst sınırlar konabildi; yani bu gazlar göz ardı edilemiyor. Ayrıca bazı ılıman alt-Neptünler için öne sürülen kükürt içeren gazlara dair net bir işaret de görülmedi. Genel olarak bu karışım, derin hidrojen atmosferine sahip ve altında belirgin bir yüzey bulunmayan Neptün benzeri bir gezegenden beklenenle uyumlu.

**İleriye Bakış**
TOI-1231 b artık bir ölçüt görevi görüyor. Gökbilimciler diğer ılıman alt-Neptünleri incelediğinde sonuçlarını bununla karşılaştırarak bir gezegenin mini-Neptün'e mi yoksa okyanus dünyası gibi daha egzotik bir şeye mi benzediğini değerlendirebilecek. Bu da söz konusu gezegenler hakkındaki iddiaları sınamayı kolaylaştırmalı.

papers.title: White dwarf planets in star clusters: gravitational scattering versus mass-loss effects
papers.abstract: White dwarfs are unique laboratories for understanding the formation, evolution and survivability of planetary systems. Post-main sequence mass-loss will change planetary orbital properties and stir up debris discs, leading to the observed pollution of white dwarf atmospheres. However, to date, very few studies have investigated the impact of the stellar birth environment on white dwarf planetary systems. In this paper we simulate the evolution of giant planets around white dwarf progenitors from their formation in a star-forming region until 1Gyr, when the most massive stars (>2M_☉) have left the main sequence. Our simulations self-consistently model N-body interactions between stars and planets while stars evolve into white dwarfs within the cluster lifetime. We find that although scattering interactions in dense star-forming regions create free-floating planets, and alter the orbital properties of up to 20 per cent of the surviving planets, the effects of mass-loss from the star dominate the dynamics. This behaviour is independent of the stellar density of the birth star-forming region, and largely independent of the initial planet orbital properties. Our simulations produce both captured planets around white dwarfs (potentially similar to WD 0806-661b), and triple systems with white dwarfs and planets (potentially similar to PSR B1620-26(AB)b), and our results yield a population synthesis of giant planets from 1 - 100au that may be relevant to Roman, Gaia and JWST observations.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
When a star like our Sun runs out of fuel, it swells up, sheds its outer layers and shrinks into a dense, glowing ember called a white dwarf. Astronomers use these stellar remnants as natural laboratories to study what happens to planets over a star's whole life. Some white dwarfs show signs of rocky debris raining onto their surfaces, which hints that planetary systems can survive, or be churned up, during this dramatic transformation. But most stars are born in crowded stellar nurseries, and very few studies have asked how that busy birthplace shapes the planets that follow.

**What They Did**
The researchers built computer simulations that follow giant planets around stars that will become white dwarfs. The simulations start when the stars form together in a star-forming region and run for 1 billion years, by which point the most massive stars (more than twice the Sun's mass) have finished their main-sequence lives. The code tracks gravitational tugs between all the stars and planets, much like a cosmic game of billiards, while the stars age and lose mass at the same time. The planets began at distances of 1 to 100 astronomical units, where one unit is the Earth–Sun distance.

**Key Findings**
Close encounters in dense clusters do matter. They kicked some planets out entirely, creating free-floating planets with no star, and changed the orbits of up to 20 per cent of the planets that stayed. Even so, the mass the stars lose as they age had the larger effect on the planets' orbits. This held true whatever the density of the birth cluster, and mostly regardless of the planets' starting orbits. The simulations also produced planets captured by white dwarfs, possibly similar to WD 0806-661b, and triple systems containing a white dwarf, another star and a planet, possibly similar to PSR B1620-26(AB)b.

**Looking Forward**

Why It Matters

When a star like our Sun runs out of fuel, it swells up, sheds its outer layers and shrinks into a dense, glowing ember called a white dwarf. Astronomers use these stellar remnants as natural laboratories to study what happens to planets over a star's whole life. Some white dwarfs show signs of rocky debris raining onto their surfaces, which hints that planetary systems can survive, or be churned up, during this dramatic transformation. But most stars are born in crowded stellar nurseries, and very few studies have asked how that busy birthplace shapes the planets that follow.

What They Did

The researchers built computer simulations that follow giant planets around stars that will become white dwarfs. The simulations start when the stars form together in a star-forming region and run for 1 billion years, by which point the most massive stars (more than twice the Sun's mass) have finished their main-sequence lives. The code tracks gravitational tugs between all the stars and planets, much like a cosmic game of billiards, while the stars age and lose mass at the same time. The planets began at distances of 1 to 100 astronomical units, where one unit is the Earth–Sun distance.

Key Findings

Close encounters in dense clusters do matter. They kicked some planets out entirely, creating free-floating planets with no star, and changed the orbits of up to 20 per cent of the planets that stayed. Even so, the mass the stars lose as they age had the larger effect on the planets' orbits. This held true whatever the density of the birth cluster, and mostly regardless of the planets' starting orbits. The simulations also produced planets captured by white dwarfs, possibly similar to WD 0806-661b, and triple systems containing a white dwarf, another star and a planet, possibly similar to PSR B1620-26(AB)b.

Looking Forward

The results give a predicted population of giant planets between 1 and 100 astronomical units that observers can compare with real data. Such comparisons may be possible with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, the Gaia mission and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

papers.title_tr: Yıldız kümelerindeki beyaz cüce gezegenleri: kütleçekimsel saçılma ve kütle kaybı etkilerinin karşılaştırması
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Güneş gibi bir yıldızın yakıtı tükendiğinde şişer, dış katmanlarını savurur ve beyaz cüce adı verilen yoğun, parlak bir közü andıran kalıntıya dönüşür. Bazı beyaz cücelerin yüzeyine kayalık enkaz yağdığına dair işaretler vardır. Bu da gezegen sistemlerinin bu çarpıcı dönüşüm sırasında ya hayatta kalabildiğini ya da altüst olduğunu düşündürür. Ancak çoğu yıldız kalabalık yıldız doğum bölgelerinde doğar ve bu hareketli doğum yerinin sonradan ortaya çıkan gezegenleri nasıl şekillendirdiğini inceleyen çok az çalışma vardır.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Araştırmacılar, ileride beyaz cüceye dönüşecek yıldızların etrafındaki dev gezegenleri izleyen bilgisayar benzetimleri kurdu. Benzetimler yıldızların bir yıldız oluşum bölgesinde birlikte doğmasıyla başlıyor ve 1 milyar yıl boyunca sürüyor. Bu sürenin sonunda en kütleli yıldızlar (Güneş'in iki katından fazla kütleli olanlar) ana kol evrelerini tamamlamış oluyor. Kod, tüm yıldızlar ile gezegenler arasındaki kütleçekimsel çekişleri, tıpkı kozmik bir bilardo oyunu gibi izlerken yıldızların yaşlanmasını ve kütle kaybetmesini de aynı anda hesaba katıyor. Gezegenler 1 ile 100 astronomik birim arasındaki uzaklıklardan başlıyor. Bir astronomik birim, Dünya ile Güneş arasındaki mesafedir.

**Ana Bulgular**
Yoğun kümelerdeki yakın karşılaşmalar önemli etkiler yarattı. Bazı gezegenler tamamen fırlatıldı ve yıldızsız, serbestçe gezen gezegenler oluştu. Kümede kalan gezegenlerin yüzde 20'sine kadarının yörüngesi değişti. Buna rağmen yıldızların yaşlanırken kaybettiği kütle, gezegen yörüngeleri üzerinde daha büyük etki yarattı. Bu durum doğum kümesinin yoğunluğundan bağımsızdı ve büyük ölçüde gezegenlerin başlangıç yörüngelerinden de bağımsızdı. Benzetimler ayrıca beyaz cüceler tarafından yakalanan gezegenler (WD 0806-661b'ye benzer olabilecek) ve bir beyaz cüce, bir başka yıldız ve bir gezegenden oluşan üçlü sistemler (PSR B1620-26(AB)b'ye benzer olabilecek) üretti.

Sonuçlar, 1 ile 100 astronomik birim arasındaki dev gezegenler için gözlemcilerin gerçek verilerle karşılaştırabileceği öngörülmüş bir nüfus sunuyor. Bu karşılaştırmalar Roman Uzay Teleskobu, Gaia ve James Webb Uzay Teleskobu (JWST) ile mümkün olabilir.

papers.title: The Mid-Infrared Transmission Spectrum of the Temperate Sub-Neptune TOI-270 d
papers.abstract: Observations of temperate sub-Neptunes with JWST have ushered in a new era for atmospheric characterization of small exoplanets. In particular, the MIRI instrument provides a unique opportunity to search for molecules that are not easily accessible in the near-infrared, as demonstrated by recent mid-infrared observations of K2-18 b. In this work, we present the first mid-infrared transmission spectrum of TOI-270 d observed using the JWST MIRI LRS (5-12 μm) instrument. By leveraging archival MIRI LRS data, we establish a new empirical relation between the detector settling timescale and the flux, which helps accurately model the spectral light curves and improve the precision of the transmission spectrum. We find that there is notable evidence of molecular features in the MIRI transmission spectrum of TOI-270 d, favouring the presence of atmospheric absorption at B = 2.8-5.3 when comparing physically plausible atmospheric models with and without molecular line absorption. The data show excess absorption beyond what could be attributed to CH₄ and CO₂ detected previously, in line with recent near-infrared results. Through an agnostic search for 203 species, we identify several candidate trace molecules, most of which are complex molecules, evaluate their physical plausibility, and compare them against inferences from near-infrared observations. We also compare the MIRI spectrum of TOI-270 d to that of K2-18 b and find that random or systematic noise is unlikely to explain these observations. Future follow-up observations are necessary to definitively identify the additional absorbers beyond CH₄ and CO₂. These observations demonstrate the unique capability of JWST MIRI for atmospheric characterisation of temperate sub-Neptunes.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Between Earth and Neptune in size lies a class of worlds called sub-Neptunes, and we have nothing like them in our own solar system. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) lets us study their atmospheres for the first time. TOI-270 d is a "temperate" sub-Neptune, meaning it is not scorching hot, which makes its air especially interesting. One of Webb's instruments, the Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI), sees wavelengths of light where many molecules leave strong fingerprints that are hard to spot with other instruments.

**What They Did**
The team measured the planet's "transmission spectrum," which is how starlight changes color as it filters through the planet's atmosphere while the planet crosses in front of its star. They used MIRI's Low Resolution Spectrometer, covering 5 to 12 micrometers. The detector behaves a bit like a camera that needs time to warm up and settle, and that drift can blur the signal. By studying older archival observations, the researchers found a new empirical relationship between how long the detector takes to settle and how bright the light is. This let them clean up the data and sharpen the spectrum. They then compared realistic atmosphere models with and without molecular absorption, and searched agnostically through 203 possible molecules.

**Key Findings**
The data favor an atmosphere with molecular absorption, at a statistical significance of about 2.8 to 5.3 "sigma" (a measure of how unlikely the result is to be a fluke). The spectrum shows more absorption than methane and carbon dioxide alone can explain, matching recent near-infrared results. The search turned up several candidate trace molecules, mostly complex ones, whose physical plausibility the team assessed. Comparing the spectrum with that of another temperate sub-Neptune, K2-18 b, the authors conclude that random or systematic noise is unlikely to explain the similarities.

**Looking Forward**
The extra absorbers are not yet identified, and the authors stress that more observations are needed to pin them down. Still, this work shows that MIRI is a powerful tool for probing the atmospheres of temperate sub-Neptunes.

papers.title_tr: Ilıman Bir Sub-Neptün Olan TOI-270 d'nin Orta Kızılötesi Geçiş Tayfı
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Boyut olarak Dünya ile Neptün arasında yer alan sub-Neptünler diye bir gezegen sınıfı var ve Güneş Sistemi'nde bunların benzeri yok. James Webb Uzay Teleskobu (JWST) sayesinde bu gezegenlerin atmosferlerini ilk kez inceleyebiliyoruz. TOI-270 d, "ılıman" yani kavurucu derecede sıcak olmayan bir sub-Neptün; bu da atmosferini özellikle ilginç kılıyor. Webb'in araçlarından biri olan Orta Kızılötesi Araç (MIRI), pek çok molekülün güçlü parmak izleri bıraktığı, diğer araçlarla görülmesi zor dalga boylarını gözlemleyebiliyor.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, gezegenin "geçiş tayfını" ölçtü. Bu, gezegen yıldızının önünden geçerken yıldız ışığının gezegenin atmosferinden süzülürken rengini nasıl değiştirdiğini gösteriyor. Araştırmacılar, MIRI'nin 5 ile 12 mikrometre arasını kapsayan Düşük Çözünürlüklü Tayfölçeri'ni kullandı. Dedektör, ısınıp oturması zaman alan bir fotoğraf makinesi gibi davranıyor ve bu kayma sinyali bulanıklaştırabiliyor. Ekip, eski arşiv gözlemlerini inceleyerek dedektörün oturma süresi ile ışığın parlaklığı arasında yeni bir deneysel ilişki buldu. Bu sayede veriyi temizleyip tayfı daha keskin hale getirdi. Ardından moleküler soğurma içeren ve içermeyen gerçekçi atmosfer modellerini karşılaştırdı ve 203 olası molekül arasında önyargısız bir arama yaptı.

**Ana Bulgular**
Veriler, yaklaşık 2,8 ile 5,3 "sigma" istatistiksel anlamlılıkla (sonucun tesadüf olma ihtimalinin ne kadar düşük olduğunu gösteren bir ölçü) moleküler soğurma içeren bir atmosferi destekliyor. Tayfta, tek başına metan ve karbondioksitle açıklanamayacak kadar fazla soğurma var; bu durum yakın zamandaki yakın kızılötesi sonuçlarla örtüşüyor. Arama sonucunda çoğu karmaşık yapılı olan birkaç aday iz molekül ortaya çıktı ve ekip bunların fiziksel olarak ne kadar makul olduğunu değerlendirdi. Yazarlar, tayfı bir başka ılıman sub-Neptün olan K2-18 b'nin tayfıyla karşılaştırdı ve benzerliklerin rastgele ya da sistematik gürültüyle açıklanmasının olası olmadığı sonucuna vardı.

**İleriye Bakış**
Ek soğurucu maddeler henüz kesin olarak belirlenemedi ve yazarlar bunları saptamak için yeni gözlemlerin gerektiğini vurguluyor. Yine de bu çalışma, MIRI'nin ılıman sub-Neptünlerin atmosferlerini incelemede güçlü bir araç olduğunu gösteriyor.

papers.title: Native-resolution retrievals of VHS 1256-1257 b spanning the JWST/NIRSpec wavelength range: Chemical composition of a partially cloudy atmosphere
papers.abstract: The wide wavelength coverage and sensitivity offered by JWST enable detailed analyses of extrasolar atmospheres. At its highest resolution (R 2700), NIRSpec measures the absorption from atomic, molecular, and isotopic gases whose abundances reflect the chemical composition of accreted material, making them key tracers of the formation environment. Orbiting an inner M-dwarf binary at a wide separation, the planetary-mass companion VHS 1256 b is one of the most variable sub-stellar objects known, with flux variations of 10-30%. We analyse the 0.97-5.27 micron NIRSpec ERS spectra of VHS 1256 b, update the data reduction and employ petitRADTRANS for atmospheric retrievals at the native spectral resolution. We model a partially cloudy atmosphere in chemical disequilibrium and fit directly for the elemental and isotopic abundances. Our best-fitting model closely matches the observations, bringing the residuals down to 1%. The results are cautiously interpreted as degeneracies can bias some parameter constraints, most notably the mass and radius. Still, the retrieval finds a partial cloud deck covering 79% of the visible surface, with a clearer column dominating at short wavelengths. Small changes of 1-3% can account for the high observed variability. From the many detected gases, we infer a metallicity, C/O ratio, and 12C/13C ratio in line with a solar composition, while the 18O isotope appears depleted relative to the Sun and local ISM. The isotope abundances are significantly lower than previous studies suggested, underlining the importance of our updated spectra. The 18O-depletion defies our understanding of the likely top-down formation. Our interpretation of the retrieved composition is complicated further by the lack of host star abundances. Nevertheless, this study demonstrates the value of panchromatic, native-resolution retrievals for characterising complex extrasolar atmospheres.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Telescopes can now do more than spot distant worlds. They can read the chemical makeup of their atmospheres, much like reading the ingredient label on a food package. Those ingredients hint at how a planet was born. VHS 1256 b is a giant planet-mass object circling a pair of small red stars at a very wide distance. It is also one of the most variable such objects known, with its brightness changing by 10-30%. That makes it a great test case for studying a complicated, patchy atmosphere.

**What They Did**
The team used data from the James Webb Space Telescope's NIRSpec instrument, which splits infrared light into a fine rainbow covering 0.97 to 5.27 microns. They updated how the raw data were processed. Then they used a computer code called petitRADTRANS to "retrieve" the atmosphere. This means adjusting a model until its light matches the observed light. They ran it at the data's full native detail. Their model included patchy clouds and chemistry that is out of balance, and it fit directly for the amounts of elements and isotopes (heavier or lighter versions of the same element).

**Key Findings**
The best model matched the observations to within about 1%. It suggests clouds cover about 79% of the visible surface, with a clearer column of atmosphere dominating at shorter wavelengths. Small changes of just 1-3% in this cloud pattern could explain the strong brightness variations. The metallicity (the share of elements heavier than hydrogen and helium), the carbon-to-oxygen ratio, and the carbon-12 to carbon-13 ratio all look similar to the Sun's. The oxygen-18 isotope, however, seems depleted compared with the Sun and nearby interstellar gas. The isotope amounts are significantly lower than earlier studies suggested. The authors urge caution, since overlapping effects can bias some results, especially the planet's mass and radius.

**Looking Forward**
The oxygen-18 shortfall is puzzling and does not fit the likely top-down formation picture, in which the object collapses from a cloud of gas like a star does. Interpretation is also hampered because the host stars' compositions are unknown. Still, the study shows that studying the full infrared range at native detail is a powerful way to probe complex alien atmospheres.

The oxygen-18 shortfall is puzzling and does not fit the likely top-down formation picture, in which the object collapses from a cloud of gas like a star does. Interpretation is also hampered because the host stars' compositions are unknown. Still, the study shows that studying the full infrared range at native detail is a powerful way to probe complex alien atmospheres.

Yazarlar, birbiriyle örtüşen etkiler bazı sonuçları, özellikle gezegenin kütlesini ve yarıçapını, yanlı hale getirebileceği için temkinli olunmasını öneriyor.

papers.title: Stellar masses and ages in Gaia Data Release 4 from the Final Luminosity Age Mass Estimator algorithm
papers.abstract: The masses and ages of stars are key quantities for understanding exoplanetary, stellar, and galactic evolution. In the context of Gaia, these parameters provide insights into the stellar populations, helping to trace the formation and history of the Galaxy. As part of the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC), the Final Luminosity Age Mass Estimator (FLAME) pipeline processes Gaia data to derive stellar parameters comprising luminosities, radii, masses and ages. This paper discusses the methods and data used in FLAME for Gaia Data releases and the expected performances of FLAME for the 4th Gaia Data Release. FLAME comprises two main components: the first one, which is analytical, is used to estimate luminosity, radius, and radial velocity correction due to gravitational redshift by exploiting the atmospheric, astrometric, and photometric parameters produced within Gaia. The second is a model inference based on two main approaches: a classical minimization approach, and a Bayesian framework. It aims to derive mass, age, and evolutionary stage. The two step implementation offers flexibility in handling photometric properties that are prone to systematic errors. Tests with simulated data, the Sun, and well characterised samples of stars show that the methods in FLAME perform as expected, producing results in statistical agreement with the literature. We provide new stellar fundamental parameters for some high velocity stars, stars with very low mass companions, and a selection of stars in the Plato Field of View. In Gaia Data Release 4 approximately 500 million sources will have results from the pipeline. [abridged]
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Imagine trying to understand a huge city's history without knowing how old its residents are or how much each one weighs. Astronomers face this problem with the Milky Way, our home galaxy. The mass and age of a star tell us where it came from, how it will live out its life, and what kinds of planets might orbit it. Gaia is a European Space Agency spacecraft that measures the positions, brightness, and colors of enormous numbers of stars. Turning those measurements into masses and ages helps trace how the Galaxy formed and changed over time. Those same numbers also matter for planet hunters, because a planet can only be understood if its star is.

**What They Did**
The team describes a software pipeline called FLAME (Final Luminosity Age Mass Estimator), part of the Gaia data-processing effort. It works in two steps. First, it uses direct calculations to work out how much light a star emits (its luminosity), how big it is (its radius), and a small correction to its measured speed caused by the star's own gravity stretching its light. Second, it compares the star with computer models of stellar evolution to infer its mass, age, and life stage. It does this in two ways: a classical "best-fit" search and a Bayesian method, which weighs how likely different answers are. Splitting the work into two steps makes it easier to handle brightness and color data that can carry systematic errors.

**Key Findings**
Tests on simulated data, on the Sun, and on well-studied stars show that FLAME performs as expected, with results statistically consistent with published values. The authors also provide new fundamental properties for some very fast-moving stars, for stars with very low-mass companions, and for a selection of stars in the field of view of Plato, a future planet-hunting mission. Gaia Data Release 4 is expected to include FLAME results for about 500 million stars.

**Looking Forward**
With hundreds of millions of stars given estimated masses and ages, astronomers will be able to build a much more detailed history of the Galaxy. Planet researchers will also gain better stellar information for the Plato mission's targets.

papers.title_tr: Final Luminosity Age Mass Estimator algoritmasından Gaia Veri Yayını 4'teki yıldız kütleleri ve yaşları
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Bir şehrin tarihini, sakinlerinin kaç yaşında olduğunu ve her birinin kaç kilo olduğunu bilmeden anlamaya çalıştığınızı düşünün. Gökbilimciler de evimiz olan Samanyolu Gökadası için aynı sorunla karşılaşıyor. Bir yıldızın kütlesi ve yaşı, onun nereden geldiğini, yaşamını nasıl sürdüreceğini ve çevresinde ne tür gezegenlerin bulunabileceğini anlatır. Gaia, çok sayıda yıldızın konumunu, parlaklığını ve rengini ölçen bir Avrupa Uzay Ajansı uzay aracıdır. Bu ölçümleri kütle ve yaşa dönüştürmek, Gökada'nın zaman içinde nasıl oluştuğunu ve değiştiğini izlememize yardımcı olur. Aynı değerler gezegen avcıları için de önemlidir, çünkü bir gezegeni ancak yıldızını bilerek anlayabiliriz.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, Gaia veri işleme çalışmasının bir parçası olan FLAME (Final Luminosity Age Mass Estimator, yani Nihai Parlaklık, Yaş ve Kütle Tahmincisi) adlı bir yazılım hattını anlatıyor. Yazılım iki adımda çalışıyor. İlk adımda doğrudan hesaplamalarla yıldızın ne kadar ışık yaydığını (ışınımgücü), ne kadar büyük olduğunu (yarıçap) ve yıldızın kendi kütleçekiminin ışığı kızıla kaydırmasından kaynaklanan küçük bir hız düzeltmesini buluyor. İkinci adımda yıldızı, yıldız evrimi bilgisayar modelleriyle karşılaştırarak kütlesini, yaşını ve yaşam evresini çıkarıyor. Bunu iki yolla yapıyor: klasik bir "en iyi uyum" araması ve farklı yanıtların olasılığını tartan Bayesçi bir yöntem. İşin iki adıma bölünmesi, sistematik hatalar taşıyabilen parlaklık ve renk verileriyle başa çıkmayı kolaylaştırıyor.

**Ana Bulgular**
Benzetim verileri, Güneş ve iyi incelenmiş yıldız örnekleri üzerinde yapılan testler, FLAME'in beklendiği gibi çalıştığını ve sonuçlarının yayımlanmış değerlerle istatistiksel olarak uyumlu olduğunu gösteriyor. Yazarlar ayrıca bazı çok hızlı yıldızlar, çok düşük kütleli eşlikçileri olan yıldızlar ve gelecekteki gezegen avcısı Plato görevinin görüş alanındaki seçilmiş yıldızlar için yeni temel özellikler sunuyor. Gaia Veri Yayını 4'ün yaklaşık 500 milyon yıldız için FLAME sonuçları içermesi bekleniyor.

**İleriye Bakış**
Yüz milyonlarca yıldıza kütle ve yaş tahmini getirilmesi, gökbilimcilerin Gökada'nın geçmişini çok daha ayrıntılı biçimde kurmasını sağlayacak. Ötegezegen araştırmacıları da Plato görevinin hedefleri için daha iyi yıldız bilgisine kavuşacak.

papers.title: GTLS: A GPU-accelerated method for periodic transit detection
papers.abstract: Computational efficiency is a critical requirement for transit searches in modern large-scale photometric surveys. We present Graphics Processing Units Transit Least Squares (GTLS), a GPU-accelerated implementation of the Transit Least Squares algorithm designed to reduce the computational cost of periodic transit detection while preserving TLS-like sensitivity to transit-shaped signals. GTLS parallelizes the dominant steps of the TLS search, including phase folding, transit-duration evaluation, moving-window depth estimation, and chi-squared calculation. Using Kepler-like long-cadence light curves and synthetic Kepler-like time series, we benchmark GTLS against the reference CPU implementation of TLS and the GPU-based BLS implementation in cuvarbase. On an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X CPU and an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU, GTLS processes a 3000-day synthetic light curve in approximately 138 seconds, compared with 3289 seconds for TLS. With two RTX 4090 GPUs, the runtime is reduced to approximately 79 seconds. In recovery tests, GTLS achieves detection performance statistically consistent with TLS, with a precision of 9.3 percent and recall of 79.4 percent, compared with 9.4 percent and 81.1 percent for TLS. These results demonstrate that GTLS enables efficient TLS-style searches for large photometric data sets from Kepler, TESS, PLATO, ET, and future missions. The source code is publicly available.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Many space telescopes watch huge numbers of stars, looking for tiny, regular dips in brightness. These dips can mean a planet is passing in front of its star, much as a moth crossing a lamp dims it briefly. Missions such as Kepler and TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) already produce enormous amounts of data, and future missions like PLATO and ET will add more. One of the most sensitive search methods, Transit Least Squares (TLS), is slow. Searching all this data with it takes a great deal of computing time.

**What They Did**
The authors built GTLS, a version of TLS that runs on graphics processing units (GPUs), the chips originally designed for video games. A GPU works like a huge crew of workers each handling a small piece of a job at once. GTLS splits the main steps of the search across that crew: lining up the data at each trial orbital period, testing different dip durations, estimating dip depth, and scoring how well each guess fits. They tested it on Kepler-like brightness records and synthetic ones, comparing it with the standard TLS on a processor (CPU) and with another GPU-based method, a Box Least Squares search in a package called cuvarbase.

**Key Findings**
On a 3000-day synthetic light curve, GTLS took about 138 seconds on one NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU. The standard TLS took 3289 seconds, so GTLS was roughly 24 times faster. With two such GPUs the time fell to about 79 seconds. In recovery tests, GTLS found planets about as well as TLS: 79.4 percent recall (the share of planted signals found) against 81.1 percent, and 9.3 percent precision (the share of detections that were correct) against 9.4 percent. The authors describe these differences as statistically consistent.

**Looking Forward**
The speedup makes TLS-style searches practical for the very large datasets from Kepler, TESS, PLATO, ET, and future missions. The authors have also made the source code publicly available, so other researchers can use and build on it.

papers.title: Understanding eccentric temperate giants: an in-depth study of the architecture and stellar obliquity of the TOI-2134 system
papers.abstract: We revisit the TOI-2134 planetary system with three new high-cadence TESS sectors and 98 more spectra. This new analysis confirms the two orbiting planets by simultaneously modelling a total of eight sectors of corrected TESS photometry and 280 HARPS-N and SOPHIE radial velocities: an inner mini-Neptune in a near-circular 9.229198±0.000003 days orbit, and an outer temperate sub-Saturn orbiting with a 95.852840±0.000042 days period and eccentricity of 0.31±0.01. The masses and radii of the planets were computed to be 9.37±0.54 Me and 2.735±0.068 Re for planet b, and 58.3±1.9 Me and 7.35±0.18 Re for planet c. The new data not only improves the detection significance and precisions on the planetary orbits, but also breaks the original multimodality in the eccentricity solution for the outer planet. We also detect a long-term trend in the radial velocity data, which we attribute to a stellar magnetic cycle. We investigate the spin-orbit alignment of the system via observations of the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect for TOI-2134 b with EXPRES and TOI-2134 c with PARAS-2. No RM effect was detected for planet b, but we find a 4.7σ detection of a 59±31ⁱrc obliquity for planet c. Finally, we examine the architecture of the system, assess its completeness, investigate the planetary interior, and their suitability for follow-up atmospheric analysis.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Many of the planets we find orbit very close to their stars. Planets on longer, cooler orbits are therefore valuable, because they help show how planetary systems form and get rearranged over time. TOI-2134 hosts two such planets, and the outer one follows a stretched, oval-shaped path. Pinning down that shape, and whether the system is tilted relative to its star's spin, gives clues to the system's past.

**What They Did**
The team revisited the system with three new high-cadence sectors of data from TESS (the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite). TESS watches for the tiny dimming of a star's light when a planet passes in front of it. They also added 98 new spectra. In total they combined eight TESS sectors with 280 radial velocity measurements from the HARPS-N and SOPHIE spectrographs, which detect the slight wobble a planet's gravity causes in its star. They also looked for the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. When a planet crosses a spinning star, it blocks part of the star's surface and subtly distorts the starlight, much like a hand passing over a spinning merry-go-round. That distortion reveals whether the orbit lines up with the star's spin. They used EXPRES for planet b and PARAS-2 for planet c.

**Key Findings**
The inner planet, TOI-2134 b, is a mini-Neptune. It circles its star every 9.23 days on a nearly circular orbit, with about 9.4 Earth masses and 2.7 times Earth's radius. The outer planet, TOI-2134 c, is a temperate sub-Saturn. It orbits every 95.85 days, has about 58 Earth masses and 7.35 times Earth's radius, and follows a clearly eccentric orbit (eccentricity 0.31). The new data resolve the earlier ambiguity in that eccentricity. The team also found a slow, long-term drift in the star's motion, which they attribute to a stellar magnetic cycle, similar to the Sun's sunspot cycle. No Rossiter-McLaughlin signal was detected for planet b. For planet c they found a 4.7σ detection, indicating a misalignment of about 59 degrees, though with a large uncertainty of ±31.

**Looking Forward**
The authors also examine the system's overall architecture, how complete our census of its planets is, what the planets' interiors might be like, and how well suited they are to future atmospheric studies.

papers.title_tr: Eksantrik ılıman devleri anlamak: TOI-2134 sisteminin mimarisi ve yıldız eğikliği üzerine derinlemesine bir çalışma
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Bulduğumuz gezegenlerin çoğu yıldızlarına çok yakın yörüngelerde dolanıyor. Bu yüzden daha uzun ve daha serin yörüngelerdeki gezegenler çok değerlidir; çünkü gezegen sistemlerinin nasıl oluştuğunu ve zamanla nasıl yeniden şekillendiğini anlamamıza yardımcı olurlar. TOI-2134 böyle iki gezegene ev sahipliği yapıyor ve dıştaki gezegen gerilmiş, oval bir yol izliyor. Bu şeklin ve sistemin yıldızın dönme eksenine göre eğik olup olmadığının belirlenmesi, sistemin geçmişine dair ipuçları verir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, sisteme yeniden baktı ve TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) uydusunun üç yeni yüksek örnekleme sıklıklı gözlem sektörünü kullandı. TESS, bir gezegen yıldızının önünden geçtiğinde yıldız ışığındaki çok küçük sönmeleri izler. Ayrıca 98 yeni tayf eklediler. Toplamda sekiz TESS sektörünü, HARPS-N ve SOPHIE tayfölçerlerinden alınan 280 radyal hız ölçümüyle birleştirdiler. Bu ölçümler, bir gezegenin kütleçekiminin yıldızında yarattığı hafif salınımı yakalar. Ayrıca Rossiter-McLaughlin etkisini aradılar. Bir gezegen dönen bir yıldızın önünden geçerken yüzeyin bir kısmını kapatır ve yıldız ışığını hafifçe bozar; tıpkı dönen bir atlıkarıncanın önünden geçen bir el gibi. Bu bozulma, yörüngenin yıldızın dönme eks†eniyle hizalı olup olmadığını ortaya koyar. Gezegen b için EXPRES, gezegen c için PARAS-2 kullanıldı.

**Ana Bulgular**
İçteki gezegen TOI-2134 b bir mini-Neptün'dür. Yıldızının etrafında 9,23 günde, neredeyse dairesel bir yörüngede dolanır; kütlesi yaklaşık 9,4 Dünya kütlesi, yarıçapı ise Dünya'nın yaklaşık 2,7 katıdır. Dıştaki gezegen TOI-2134 c ise ılıman bir alt-Satürn'dür. 95,85 günde bir dolanır, yaklaşık 58 Dünya kütlesine ve Dünya yarıçapının 7,35 katına sahiptir; yörüngesi belirgin biçimde eksantriktir (eksantriklik 0,31). Yeni veriler, eksantriklikteki önceki belirsizliği ortadan kaldırdı. Ekip ayrıca yıldızın hareketinde yavaş, uzun vadeli bir sürüklenme buldu ve bunu Güneş'in leke döngüsüne benzer bir yıldız manyetik döngüsüne bağlıyor. Gezegen b için Rossiter-McLaughlin sinyali saptanmadı. Gezegen c için ise 4,7σ'lık bir tespit yapıldı; bu, yaklaşık 59 derecelik bir hizasızlığa işaret ediyor, ancak belirsizlik büyük (±31).

**İleriye Bakış**
Yazarlar ayrıca sistemin genel mimarisini, gezegen sayımımızın ne kadar eksiksiz olduğunu, gezegenlerin iç yapılarının nasıl olabileceğini ve gelecekteki atmosfer çalışmalarına ne kadar uygun olduklarını inceliyor.

papers.title: Stellar Forcing of (exo)Planetary Environments
papers.abstract: The environments of exoplanets are fundamentally shaped by the magnetic activity of their host stars through a combination of radiative, plasma, and particle-driven processes. This article presents a comprehensive overview of the four principal forms of stellar forcing that regulate atmospheric structure, chemistry, escape, and long-term planetary evolution: high-energy radiation, magnetized stellar winds, coronal mass ejections, and energetic particles. Using the Sun as a physically resolved benchmark, the discussion extends toward increasingly active cool stars to establish a broader picture for star--planet interactions across the main sequence. The article first examines the production of stellar X-ray and extreme ultraviolet emission from chromospheres and coronae, together with the variability introduced by flares and, more generally, magnetic reconnection processes. Particular attention is given to spectroscopic diagnostics, activity scalings with stellar rotation and age, flare energetics, statistical flare behavior, and the observational connections between impulsive and gradual phases of magnetic energy release. The treatment then shifts to the continuous outflow of magnetized plasma, describing the thermodynamic and magnetic mechanisms that drive stellar winds and the role of multidimensional magnetohydrodynamic modeling in determining wind structure, angular momentum loss, and planetary interaction regimes. Solar and stellar coronal mass ejections are subsequently explored through their observational diagnostics, flare associations, propagation properties, and possible suppression by strong stellar magnetic fields. Finally, the transport and modulation of galactic and stellar energetic particles are discussed, together with current approaches for estimating particle environments in active planetary systems and their consequences for atmospheric chemistry and climate. The article concludes by outlining future observational and numerical developments required to connect these coupled stellar forcing processes within a unified exoplanetary framework.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Planets do not sit quietly in space. Every planet orbits a star, and stars with active magnetic fields, like our Sun, constantly bombard their planets with energy and matter. Think of a campfire: the closer you sit, and the more it crackles and spits sparks, the harder it is to stay comfortable. For planets around other stars, this "stellar forcing" can shape whether an atmosphere survives, what chemicals it contains, and even whether the climate could support life. This matters most for planets orbiting small, active stars, which are the easiest targets for finding Earth-sized worlds.

**What They Did**
This review article gathers what scientists know about four main ways a star affects its planets. The first is high-energy light, namely X-rays and extreme ultraviolet light, including sudden bursts called flares. The second is stellar wind, a steady stream of magnetized gas flowing off the star. The third is coronal mass ejections, giant eruptions of plasma. The fourth is energetic particles, fast-moving charged bits of matter. The authors use the Sun, which we can study in great detail, as a benchmark. They then extend the picture to more active cool stars, drawing on observations, computer simulations, and how activity changes with a star's spin and age.

**Key Findings**
Because this is an overview, it presents a framework rather than a single new discovery. It shows that these four forms of forcing are linked, all driven by magnetic energy being released in a star's outer layers. It also covers how stellar winds carry away angular momentum, and how strong magnetic fields may suppress coronal mass ejections. It reviews how particle environments around active stars can be estimated, along with their effects on atmospheric chemistry and climate.

**Looking Forward**
The authors conclude that future observations and more advanced computer models are needed to connect these processes into one unified picture of how stars shape the environments of exoplanets.

**Neden Önemli**
Gezegenler uzayda sessizce durmaz. Her gezegen bir yıldızın yörüngesindedir ve Güneş gibi manyetik olarak etkin yıldızlar, gezegenlerini sürekli enerji ve madde yağmuruna tutar. Bir kamp ateşini düşünün: ateşe ne kadar yakın oturursanız ve ateş ne kadar çok çıtırdayıp kıvılcım saçarsa, rahat etmek o kadar zorlaşır. Diğer yıldızların etrafındaki gezegenler için bu "yıldızsal zorlama", bir atmosferin ayakta kalıp kalmayacağını, hangi kimyasalları içereceğini ve iklimin yaşamı destekleyip destekleyemeyeceğini belirleyebilir. Bu durum, Dünya boyutunda gezegenleri bulmak için en kolay hedefler olan küçük ve etkin yıldızların çevresindeki gezegenler için özellikle önemlidir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Bu derleme makale, bir yıldızın gezegenlerini etkilediği dört ana yolla ilgili bilinenleri bir araya getiriyor. Birincisi, X-ışınları ve aşırı mor ötesi ışık gibi yüksek enerjili ışınımdır; buna patlama adı verilen ani parlamalar da dahildir. İkincisi, yıldızdan sürekli akan manyetize gaz olan yıldız rüzgârıdır. Üçüncüsü, dev plazma püskürmeleri olan koronal kütle atımlarıdır. Dördüncüsü ise hızlı hareket eden yüklü parçacıklar olan enerjik parçacıklardır. Yazarlar, ayrıntılı biçimde inceleyebildiğimiz Güneş'i ölçüt olarak kullanıyor. Ardından gözlemlerden, bilgisayar benzetimlerinden ve etkinliğin yıldızın dönüşü ve yaşıyla nasıl değiştiğinden yararlanarak resmi daha etkin serin yıldızlara genişletiyor.

**Ana Bulgular**
Bu bir derleme olduğu için tek bir yeni keşiften çok bir çerçeve sunuyor.
